# Incident Report — 2024-11-26 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Evidence reviewed
- `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (26,922 frames, 04:49:38–05:43:58 UTC)
- `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.txt` (Suricata/ET alert export)
- `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.png` (screenshot of the same alerts)

## Victim host
| Field | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.11.26.183** | Consistent across all evidence |
| MAC | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** | ARP (`arp.src.proto_ipv4`/`arp.src.hw_mac`) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** | NBNS (`DESKTOP-B8TQK49<00>`/`<20>`) and mDNS/LLMNR |
| AD/NetBIOS domain | NEMOTODES / `nemotoads.health` | NBNS `NEMOTODES<1e>` browser election; DNS SRV lookups for `nemotoads.health` |
| Logged-in user | **oboomwald** | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ issued by 10.11.26.183 |
| Domain controller (context) | NEMOTODE-DC, 10.11.26.3, MAC 00:24:e8:7f:09:5d | NBNS, ARP, DNS (`NEMOTODES-DC.nemotoads.health`) |
| Gateway (context) | 10.11.26.1, MAC 00:17:e0:b8:29:5e | ARP |

## Malware family
**NetSupport RAT** (the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-support client abused as a commodity RAT).

**Attribution: signature-confirmed AND protocol-confirmed.**
- Suricata alerts fired directly on the C2 traffic: `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`, `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Response`, `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`.
- Independently confirmed in the raw traffic: the beacon HTTP requests carry `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`, the server responds with `Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.8 (Windows NT)`, and the body uses the literal NetSupport client-gateway protocol fields `CMD=POLL`, `CMD=ENCD`, `ES=1`, `DATA=<encrypted blob>` (verified via `tshark -z follow,tcp,ascii` on stream 77).

## Timeline
1. **04:50:14–04:50:40 UTC** — 10.11.26.183 resolves `modandcrackedapk.com` → `193.42.38.139` (flagged `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain`, a known cracked-software/piracy lure category), then opens a TLS session to that IP with SNI `modandcrackedapk.com`. This is the delivery/lure stage. The payload transfer itself is inside TLS and not recoverable from this capture (no session keys), so no dropper file/hash can be grounded from the pcap.
2. **04:50:45 UTC** — NetSupport client performs a one-time self-geolocation lookup: `GET /location/loca.asp` to `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` (104.26.1.231), response `33.7488,-84.3877`. This is NetSupport's own legitimate infrastructure (benign context, not a C2 indicator), but its use confirms a genuine NetSupport Manager binary is running.
3. **04:50:45 UTC through end of capture (05:43:58 UTC)** — Persistent C2 beaconing: HTTP POST to `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` roughly every 60 seconds, `CMD=POLL`/`CMD=ENCD` checkins with encrypted `DATA` payloads, confirming an active, ongoing RAT session with the attacker's gateway.

## Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in the capture)

**Command-and-control**
- `194.180.191.64:443` — NetSupport RAT C2 (plaintext HTTP carried on port 443), endpoint `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm`, ~65+ beacon POSTs over the capture window.

**Malicious/lure domain**
- `modandcrackedapk.com` → resolves to `193.42.38.139` — cracked-software lure site, delivery vector for the RAT.

**Malicious URL**
- `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` — C2 checkin URL.

**Files/hashes**
- No malware executable or archive was transferred in cleartext anywhere in this capture. The only objects recoverable via HTTP object export are benign OS/browser telemetry (`connecttest.txt`, `ProcessMAU.txt`, OCSP/CRL blobs, the tiny `fakeurl.htm`/`loca.asp` C2 protocol bodies). The initial payload was delivered inside the TLS session to `193.42.38.139` and cannot be hashed from this evidence.

**Benign context observed (not IOCs)**
- `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` (104.26.1.231) — legitimate NetSupport vendor infrastructure used by the client's own geolocation feature.
- The `ETPRO [MS-EFSR]`/`GPL NETBIOS SMB ... overflow attempt`/`IPC$` alerts against the DC (10.11.26.3) are standard AD/SMB1 domain chatter (NULL-session NTLMSSP, no exploitation evidence) and are old, high-false-positive-rate GPL signatures; not asserted as malicious.
- `classicgrand.com`, `confirmsubscription.com`, `createsend1.com` — email/marketing-tracker TLS SNIs seen in the traffic mix, no alert or C2 behavior tied to them; unrelated to the infection.

## Summary
DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (10.11.26.183, MAC d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b), logged in as domain user **oboomwald** on the NEMOTODES/nemotoads.health domain, visited the cracked-software lure site `modandcrackedapk.com` (193.42.38.139) and was infected with **NetSupport RAT**. The malware immediately began persistent C2 beaconing to **194.180.191.64:443** (`/fakeurl.htm`), confirmed both by Suricata ETPRO signatures and by direct inspection of the NetSupport client/gateway protocol strings in the traffic. The initial payload itself was delivered over TLS and could not be extracted or hashed from this capture.
